findings.reason: The protected solution is concise, conventional, and interview-ready. The color, result, start, value, and digit names expose channel parsing, shorthand rounding, and output construction directly, with no generic local named index.

A repeated hexadecimal digit d represents the byte 16d + d = 17d, so every shorthand-expressible channel is one of the 16 multiples of 17. The similarity objective is the negative sum of three independent squared channel errors, making its global maximum exactly the combination of the nearest valid value for each channel. For byte value v, (v + 8) // 17 rounds to the nearest multiple's digit: adjacent levels are 17 apart, their midpoint is a half-integer, and an integer byte therefore has no tie. Values from 0 through 255 map within digit indices 0 through 15. Parsing each channel, formatting the selected digit in lowercase, repeating it twice, and retaining the leading hash produces the unique optimal six-digit color.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 800, Python, and the native similarRGB(color) interface. Authenticated source evidence confirms a seven-character #RRGGBB input, a leading hash, lowercase hexadecimal digits after it, #XYZ shorthand expanding to #XXYYZZ, similarity as the negative sum of three squared channel differences, and a six-digit shorthand-expressible return. The statement accepts any co-optimal answer; because adjacent repeated-digit bytes differ by 17, an integer channel cannot tie, so the protected solution still returns the unique optimum.

The protected app source and immutable native source bound to verified submission 2066208742 are algorithmically identical: both inspect channel starts 1, 3, and 5, parse the same hexadecimal bytes, compute the same (value + 8) // 17 digit, format it in lowercase, repeat it, prepend a hash, and join the result. Their only structural difference is the required Solution.similarRGB wrapper.

The authenticated contract fixes every legal input at exactly three two-digit channels, so it provides no source workload dimension for an honest runtime trend. The previous synthetic tier size measured how many shorthand levels one chosen alternative inspected rather than an input parameter and was removed. A strict bounded-domain certificate records C = 3 channels, the finite 256-value byte domain, and the absence of scalable input width. Fresh independent validation checked every byte value in each channel position, all 4096 shorthand fixed points, 5000 random legal colors, and 100 complete searches over all 4096 shorthand candidates. The permanent regression independently checks all 768 byte-position combinations against a nearest-candidate oracle and confirms both protected sources. The exact app source also passed all 10 correctness cases through real-test with O(1) reported explicitly and no runtime benchmark claim.

The Approach accurately derives repeated-digit bytes as multiples of 17, separates the squared objective by channel, proves uniqueness from the odd gap between candidates, explains arithmetic rounding and formatting, and covers boundary values. Its O(1) time and O(1) auxiliary-space claims match the protected implementation and branch manifest.

The modular Reference preserves the shorthand definition and source expansion example, the exact negative squared-channel similarity formula, the co-optimal-answer rule, both source examples in order, all three constraints, and the complete two-step numerical explanation attached only to Example 1. The invented third source-labelled example was removed.

A fresh authenticated Premium review verified exactly two examples, an explanation only for Example 1, three constraints, and no hints, notes, images, tables, diagrams, or follow-up. The modular files are hash-bound in source_fidelity.json to source content hash d6883320c514da3d58d91f295c7ed7770f94d5e18fe2d8923a54464cca7c83ac, and the direct fidelity validator returns verified with no errors.

coverage: The authenticated Premium statement contains exactly two examples. Both exact input and output pairs now appear first in source order, and the formerly source-labelled #abcdef conversion is retained only as a separately labelled trial.

All 10 ordinary correctness cases are visible samples or trials. They cover the fixed seven-character form, lower and upper channel bytes 00 and ff, lowercase hexadecimal letters, exact shorthand channels, and the lower 08/09 and upper f6/f7 rounding transitions.

Material behavior includes all three independent channel positions, mixed upward and downward rounding, exact middle-range values, distinct red/green/blue values, preservation of the leading hash and lowercase six-digit formatting, and the odd-gap fact that eliminates nearest-candidate ties for integer bytes.
An independent brute-force oracle chooses the closest of all sixteen repeated-digit channel values and recomputed every authored expected result without using the protected arithmetic formula.

The independent oracle, protected app source, and immutable native Solution agreed on all 10 authored cases, every one of the 256 byte values in each of the three channel positions, all 4096 shorthand fixed points, and 5000 deterministic random legal colors. One hundred random colors were also checked by globally enumerating all 4096 shorthand candidates; the protected app source passed the complete real-test path.

The package has no scaling benchmark because the source contract fixes the workload at exactly three channels. The misleading algorithm-dependent tiers were removed, and a strict bounded-domain certificate plus permanent exhaustive per-channel regression now supplies the required complexity evidence without exposing correctness inputs as performance workloads.
